scope: Selected cross-cutting ECC harness evidence: root policy and packaging, representative canonical skills/agents, capability-surface guidance, selected context manifests, and evaluation/hook integration examples. This is not a deep review of the full multi-harness catalog.

limits: Recursive Git tree was complete (6,674 entries; not truncated), with no submodule or symlink entries; 46 binary-named assets were indexed but not fetched.
Deep review was bounded to representative cross-cutting files; the source has 327 canonical skill entries, 72 agents, 98 legacy commands, and many platform-specific mirrors/adapters.
Most hook handlers, 37-server MCP manifest details, the module installer map, and transitive memory/eval libraries remain indexed only; no package was installed and no source code was executed.
No external link was followed. Credential-related evidence records environment-variable names only, never values.
next: Review the complete canonical skill/agent catalog and map duplicates/adaptations across .agents, .claude, .cursor, .codex, .opencode, and other harness adapters.
Trace the complete hook graph, its validators, and transitive session/memory helpers before considering any hook or memory runtime.
Inspect the install-modules registry and selected MCP server configurations/packages; verify per-server permissions and required credentials before any integration.
Review all eval-harness library modules and tests before importing any CLI behavior; execution remains unavailable until independently verified OS containment exists.
